questions.q: Minimum volume of water an interior wet standpipe should provide. (sec 1212.3.b)
questions.n: This is the minimum required flow rate for wet standpipes to ensure adequate water supply for fire hoses.

questions.q: Minimum volume of water an interior dry standpipe should provide. (sec 1212.3.b)
questions.n: Dry standpipes must provide this volume to support heavy-duty firefighting operations from external sources.

questions.q: Minimum diameter of a wet standpipe. (sec 1212.2.b.i)
questions.n: The code specifies a 2-inch minimum diameter for the standpipe itself to maintain pressure.

questions.q: Standard diameter of a dry standpipe opening. (sec 1212.2.f)
questions.n: The standard opening diameter for dry standpipes is 2 1/2 inches to accommodate standard fire hoses.

questions.q: Standard length of a fire hose (sec 1212.3.c & j)
questions.n: Section 1212 specifies 23 meters as the standard length for fire hoses in building systems.

questions.q: Maximum distance of a hose nozzle to any portion of a building. (sec 1212.3.c)
questions.n: The code allows for a 6.00-meter reach from the nozzle to ensure full coverage of the floor area.

questions.q: Standard diameter of a wet standpipe valve. (sec 1212.3.e)
questions.n: This is the standard valve diameter for wet standpipes, designed for occupant use.

questions.q: Maximum projection into a non-arcaded sidewalk of a signboard. (sec 2004.1.d)
questions.n: For non-arcaded sidewalks, signboards may project up to 1.20 meters.

questions.q: Maximum projection into a arcaded sidewalk of a signboard. (sec 2004.1.d.i)
questions.n: In arcaded sidewalks, the projection is halved compared to non-arcaded ones to maintain clearance.

questions.q: Minimum vertical clearance from the bottom of a signage to an arcaded sidewalk. (sec 2004.1.d.ii)
questions.n: The code requires 5.00 meters of clearance under signs in arcaded areas.

questions.q: Minimum vertical clearance from the bottom of a signage to non-arcaded sidewalk. (sec 2004.1.d.ii)
questions.n: A minimum of 3.00 meters is required for signs over non-arcaded sidewalks.

questions.q: Number of days of work abandonment or stoppage for a building permit to expire. (sec 305)
questions.n: A permit expires if work is abandoned or suspended for 120 days.

questions.q: Width of planting strip for sidewalks 2.00 mts in width. (sec 811.D.9)
questions.n: For a 2.00-meter sidewalk, an 0.80-meter planting strip is mandated.

questions.q: Minimum horizontal distance of the curb line to the outermost face of an arcade. (fig. VIII.G.14)
questions.n: The code requires a 500mm (0.5m) setback from the curb line to the arcade face.

questions.q: Slope of ramp of road-way to driveway. (sec 8112.12.a.i)
questions.n: The required slope range for this specific transition is 1/3 to 1/4.

questions.q: Slope of driveway to sidewalk where the height of curb is 200 mm and above. (sec 8112.12.a.i)
questions.n: A 1:8 slope is required when the curb height is 200mm or higher.

questions.q: Min. clearance of conductors from any platform or ground or projection from w/c they might be reached.
questions.n: A 3.00-meter clearance is needed to prevent accidental contact from reachable areas.

questions.q: Minimum clearance of conductors from the highest point of a roof. (sec 1301.5)
questions.n: The code mandates 2.50 meters of clearance from the highest roof point.

questions.q: Min. vertical cl. of service drop lines above ground at its point of attachment to the building. (sec 1301.5.d)
questions.n: Service drops must be at least 3.00 meters above the ground at the point of attachment.

questions.q: Min. Vertical cl. of a service drop communication line when crossing a street. (sec 1301.5.d)
questions.n: A minimum vertical clearance of 5.50 meters is required when crossing a street.

questions.q: Minimum width of an access road to a cul-de-sac. (fig VIII. G.7)
questions.n: The minimum width for an access road to a cul-de-sac is 3.00 meters.

questions.q: Unit area per occupant for Dwellings.
questions.n: Dwellings are calculated at 28.00 square meters per occupant.

questions.q: Unit area per occupant for Hotels, Dormitories & Apartments.
questions.n: The occupant load factor for hotels, dorms, and apartments is 18.6 sqm per person.

questions.q: Unit area per occupant for Offices and Garages.
questions.n: Offices and garages use a factor of 9.30 square meters per occupant.

questions.q: Unit area per occupant for Classrooms.
questions.n: Classrooms are calculated based on 1.80 square meters per occupant.

questions.q: Unit area per occupant for Stores, Retail sales rooms upper floors.
questions.n: Upper floor retail spaces are calculated at 5.60 square meters per person.

questions.q: Unit area per occupant for Stores, Retail sales rooms @ the Basements & Ground Flr.
questions.n: Basements and ground floors of stores use 2.80 square meters per occupant.

questions.q: Unit area per occupant for Nurseries for children.
questions.n: Nurseries for children require 3.25 square meters per occupant.

questions.q: Unit area per occupant for Home for the aged.
questions.n: Homes for the aged use an occupant load factor of 7.40 square meters.

questions.q: Unit area for Hospitals and Sanitaria.
questions.n: Hospitals and sanitaria are calculated at 8.40 square meters per person.

questions.q: Unit area per occupant for aircraft hangars without repairs.
questions.n: Hangars without repairs have a low density of 46.50 square meters per person.

questions.q: Unit area per occupant for warehouses and mechanical equipment room.
questions.n: Warehouses and mechanical rooms are calculated at 28.00 square meters per person.

questions.q: Unit area per occupant for Auditoriums, theaters, Dance floor, Churches and the likes.
questions.n: Concentrated assembly areas use 0.65 square meters per occupant.

questions.q: Minimum exits for 1st floor and above with occupant load of more than 10.
questions.n: A minimum of two exits is required for floors with more than 10 occupants.

questions.q: One or more habitable rooms which are occupied or intended to be occupied by one family with facilities for cooking, sleeping, living, and eating
questions.n: This is the official NBCP definition for a room or group of rooms for one family.

questions.q: That portion of the foundation of a structure which spreads and transmits loads directly to the ground or soil.
questions.n: The footing is specifically designed to distribute structural loads into the soil.

questions.q: A continuous horizontal layer of masonry units.
questions.n: A 'course' refers to a single horizontal layer of bricks or stones.

questions.q: A room or suite of two or more rooms, designed and intended for, or occupied by one family for living, sleeping, eating, and cooking purposes.
questions.n: The code defines an apartment as a suite of two or more rooms for one family.

questions.q: A stationary open hearth or brazier, either fuel-fired or electric, used for food preparation.
questions.n: The NBCP defines this stationary hearth specifically as a barbecue.

questions.q: A portion of the seating space of an assembly room, the lowest part of which is raised 1.20 mts or more above the level of the main floor.
questions.n: The code defines a balcony in an assembly room as being raised at least 1.20m.

questions.q: The pipe which connects a flue-burning appliance to a chimney.
questions.n: This is the specific technical term for the bridging pipe to the chimney.

questions.q: A hearth & fire chamber or similarly prepared place in w/c a fire may be made & w/c is built in conjunction w/ a chimney.
questions.n: A fireplace is the built-in chamber used for making fires in conjunction with a chimney.

questions.q: A horizontal structural piece which supports the end of the floor beams or joists or walls over opening.
questions.n: Girders are primary horizontal supports that carry the load of other beams/joists.

questions.q: Same as heliport except that no refueling, maintenance, repairs, or storage of helicopters is permitted.
questions.n: A helistop is a landing area without the support services of a full heliport.

questions.q: A term which may be used synonymously with a partition.
questions.n: In structural and architectural terms, a cross wall can be synonymous with a partition.

questions.q: The vertical supports, such as posts or stanchions, as used in indigenous or traditional type of construction.
questions.n: The NBCP uses 'suportales' to describe traditional vertical supports.

questions.q: Any surface or underground construction covered on top, or any fire-proof construction intended for the storage of valuables.
questions.n: A vault is a fire-proof construction used specifically for storing valuables.

questions.q: Front yards for commercial buildings abutting a road-right-of-way of 25-29 meters shall have a minimum width....
questions.n: For an RROW of 25-29 meters, a front yard of 8.00 meters is required.

questions.q: Offices shall be provided how many cubic meters of air per person? (sec 807.b)
questions.n: The code requires 12.00 cubic meters of air per person for office spaces.

questions.q: Multiple living units of up to 6 units built on the same lot shall have an access road directly connecting said building to a public street w/ a minimum width of how many meters? (table VIII.G.3)
questions.n: Up to 6 units on a single lot require a 3.00-meter wide access road.
